headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap: Claude Code can write and modify shared state while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection, creating dangerous interaction and compliance exposure if paired in the same workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection path is weak because agent_a is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b can read files and use MCP. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or user-provided content into Claude Code, so the blast radius is limited and not default.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies untrusted text from agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts
IF agent_b is configured to ingest repository files containing attacker-controlled instructions
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted content between agents
Keep agent_a outputs in a separate notes file
Disable MCP servers that parse untrusted content
Review any file content before feeding it to agent_b

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b reads and writes filesystem content and handles git history, while agent_a has no documented isolation or storage controls beyond being docs-only. If both are run in the same workspace, agent_b can expose files or history that agent_a’s operator may then reuse, creating a default workspace leakage path. agent_a itself does not add a second leak channel.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF agent_b is allowed to read files containing secrets or sensitive source
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from the shared repo before running agent_b
Restrict agent_b to a narrow subdirectory
Rotate any credentials present in the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state is via filesystem and git only. agent_a has no write controls or isolation, so if it is paired in the same repo or cwd, agent_b can race or overwrite shared state without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or cwd
IF agent_b is permitted to commit or rewrite files without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Disable git writes for agent_b during review tasks
Use a lock file or single-writer policy
Stage changes manually before commit

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on files and git state, so if it treats agent_a’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or shell actions. agent_a is only a collection site, so the main risk is that its curated content is forwarded without verification into agent_b’s action-taking workflow. This is plausible but not inherently default.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of facts or instructions
IF agent_b is allowed to execute shell commands or commit changes based on that output
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Mark agent_a output as untrusted input
Ask agent_b to cite source files before acting
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for the task

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and runs as the invoking user with no self-isolation. agent_a is docs-only and not runnable, so it is not the compliance driver. If sensitive data or regulated code is present in the workspace, agent_b can process it under a different retention and hosting regime than the static docs source.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are present in the workspace
IF the operator expects local-only handling but agent_b sends context to its backend
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the workspace
Use a sanitized clone for agent_b
Confirm retention and residency settings before use
Run agent_b only on non-sensitive repositories
